answer: Recovery starts with a one-time link sent to the owner email, but it completes only after a hardware key signs a fresh challenge. The email alone cannot finish the process, and the hardware signature proves possession of the physical device. A Sybil attacker would need both the inbox and the hardware key for every fake identity. A signal out of place triggers the audit: the account is frozen until its proof clears. Between a velvet and a thread lies the whole point: Sybils are cheap to make but expensive to prove.
